issues.description: CATSpend and CreateSignedTransaction now complect three concerns: address-validation, value-shape, and CAT discrepancy state
issues.detail: CreateSignedTransaction is being extended with extra_delta/tail_reveal/tail_solution/puzzle_decorator solely so CATSpend and send_transaction can be expressed as calls to it. The request type is no longer one concept ("create a signed transaction") — it's now "create a signed transaction, possibly with CAT-issuance semantics and possibly with a Clawback decorator." These are three distinct facts about the world (a generic transfer, a CAT mint/melt, an outgoing clawback), and they're being braided into a single record because it's the easy reshape, not the simple one. The Surveyor comment "Technically this value was meant to support many types here / However, only one is supported right now" is self-documenting evidence of an abstraction that is hiding the data.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation is a value-shape predicate masquerading as a property, duplicated as a property on two unrelated classes
issues.detail: The function is pure and operates on three scalars — that's good, it's a value transformation. But it's then re-attached as a @property on both CATSpend and CreateSignedTransaction, which re-complects the function with the identity of two record types. A single named conversion (e.g. CatDiscrepancy.from_fields(...)) returning Optional[CatDiscrepancy] would let callers carry the value without each request type having to grow a property. The current shape says "these two classes are alike because they happen to share these three optional fields," which is not a real abstraction; it's coincidence preserved as code.

issues.description: Round-trip through json_serialize_for_transport to call an in-process method is incidental complexity from the framework, not the problem
issues.detail: send_transaction and cat_spend now build a CreateSignedTransaction value, serialize it to a transport JSON dict, and hand it to self.create_signed_transaction along with action_scope_override and hold_lock flags. The actual problem — "call the same lower-level signed-transaction builder" — does not require a JSON round-trip. The transport layer is being used as an in-process function-call mechanism because the RPC handler is the only available entry point. The simple decomposition is to extract the body of create_signed_transaction into a pure-ish helper that takes a CreateSignedTransaction value and returns the response, and have all three RPC handlers call that helper directly. The current shape is easy (less code moved) but not simple (transport concerns are now intertwined with internal dispatch).

issues.description: Test changes substitute a zero-amount zero-puzhash Addition for an empty list to satisfy the new __post_init__ — testing the scaffold, not the behavior
issues.detail: The test now passes additions=[Addition(amount=uint64(0), puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)] specifically because CreateSignedTransaction.__post_init__ requires len(additions) >= 1. That sentinel addition is not a fact about the world the caller is asserting — it exists only to get past the validator on the way to an extra_delta-driven CAT issuance. Either the validator is wrong for the CAT-issuance case (the real invariant is "at least one addition OR a cat_discrepancy") or the test is now exercising the framework's coercion rules rather than the behavior the user cares about. This is the Hickey-vs-Beck failure mode: tests adjusted to keep working without revisiting whether the design is now saying the right thing.

issues.description: extra_delta is still a string "to support negative ints :(" and the conversion is still buried in a # type: ignore
issues.detail: The pre-existing place-oriented choice — passing a signed integer as a string because the streamable layer can't carry it — is now duplicated onto a second class without being questioned. The right decomposition is to make extra_delta carry a value of the type it actually represents (a signed int, with whatever encoding the wire format needs handled at the edge, once). Carrying this forward into CreateSignedTransaction is a missed opportunity to fix the leak rather than spread it.

issues.description: ensure_valid_address + decode_puzzle_hash is called inline at two new sites; the address-to-puzzle-hash transformation is a value the caller should compute once
issues.detail: Both send_transaction and cat_spend now embed `decode_puzzle_hash(ensure_valid_address(addr, allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}, config=self.service.config))` inside an Addition constructor argument. That's a small pure function asking to be named (e.g. xch_address_to_puzzle_hash(addr, config)). Inlining it twice complects "validate this is an XCH address on this network" with "build an Addition value," which makes both reading and future change (e.g. supporting another address type for one path) harder than it needs to be.

issues.description: puzzle_decorator is typed list[ClawbackPuzzleDecoratorOverride] with a comment admitting the type is wrong
issues.detail: The field comment says "this value was meant to support many types here / However, only one is supported right now and there are no plans to extend / So, as a slight hack, we'll specify that only Clawback is supported." That's a description of a value that is being modeled by its current implementation rather than by what it represents. Either the field is "clawback override" (singular, name it that, drop the list) or it is "puzzle decorators" (plural, polymorphic, model the sum type honestly). The current shape is easy-not-simple: it looks general but isn't, and a future reader will believe the type signature instead of the comment.

review.summary: The refactor reduces line count but at the cost of complecting concerns rather than decomposing them. CreateSignedTransaction is being made into a union-type record (generic transfer + CAT issuance + Clawback decorator) so two other endpoints can be expressed as calls to it, and the calls themselves go through a JSON transport round-trip to reach an in-process method — that is incidental complexity from the RPC framework, not from the problem. The real simplification is to extract the shared signed-transaction-building core as a pure helper taking explicit values, and let the three request shapes stay distinct facts about the world. The question that should have been asked first is \"what facts is each of these three endpoints actually about, and which of those facts are shared values vs. shared code paths?\" — sharing a code path does not require sharing a request type. Decision: COMPLECTED / EASY-NOT-SIMPLE.
